question: Should default `/status` and `openclaw status` show exact transcript-summed cost by scanning full transcripts, or require a bounded/precomputed cost aggregate before this feature lands?
rationale: The user-visible direction is clear, but the active implementation has a maintainer-visible tradeoff between exact cumulative cost and preserving the fast status path for large transcripts.

options.title: Keep Status Bounded
options.body: Require the implementation to use a bounded read, persisted session aggregate, or maintained aggregate so ordinary status remains responsive while showing cost.

options.title: Accept Exact Full Scan
options.body: Allow the status paths to scan full transcripts for exact cumulative cost and document the responsiveness tradeoff for long sessions.

options.title: Defer For Aggregate Storage
options.body: Pause the feature until broader session aggregate storage work provides a canonical cheap cost source.

recommendation.title: Keep Status Bounded
recommendation.body: Require the implementation to use a bounded read, persisted session aggregate, or maintained aggregate so ordinary status remains responsive while showing cost.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has recent history in the status rendering path where this UX/performance tradeoff lands.
